summary: Wenbiao Mai is an indologist and linguist who studied at Peking University, earning a PhD, as well as the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University. He was attested as a guest assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong in 2013.

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Stanford University in 1998, studying under Michel Strickmann, Seizan Yanagida, Hidehiko Koga, and Chizuko Inui, and held posts at Barnard College and the University of Calgary.

Wendy Doniger is a scholar of indology, religious studies, and history. She earned degrees from Radcliffe College, Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and Oxford University under Robert Charles Zaehner, later serving at the University of Chicago from 1978 to 2018.
Wenjiang Ding (1887–1936) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under Qichao Liang and at Peking University. He held an academic post at Peking University from circa 1930 to 1933.

Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts. He held multiple leadership posts at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946 through 1998 and at Tokyo University of the Arts.

Wenjie Qin is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming, also studying under Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who studied at TU Wien, Innsbruck, and the University of Vienna, where he completed his PhD in 1965. He held posts at Illinois, Tübingen, and an ordinary professorship at the University of Groningen from 1971.

Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He held posts at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1967–1991), the University of Berlin (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
Wes Borton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Derek F. Maher at East Carolina University and later studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1970–1975), later holding posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of California, Davis.

Whitney Cox specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1999–2006), and held posts at the University of Chicago and SOAS University of London (~2006–2013).

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne (1928–1986) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned a PhD from SOAS/University of London, later holding faculty and dean positions at the universities of Ceylon, Peradeniya, and Kelaniya.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He completed a master's program at the University of Colorado and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar. Educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton (PhD ~1946–1948), he held major academic posts at Forman Christian College, McGill University, Dalhousie University, Harvard University (1964–1973, 1978–1985), and Trinity College, Toronto.

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher who studied at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and held a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) was a linguist who earned his Dr. phil. at Leipzig and studied at Berlin under Weber, Bopp, Schott, and Haupt. He served as a school director and teacher at Katharineum, Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Jean Sturm, Gymnasium Buchsweiler, and Lycée de Mulhouse.

Wilhelm Dilthey (1833–1911) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Heidelberg (~1852–1853) and Berlin (~1853–1856). He held academic posts at the universities of Basel, Kiel, Breslau, and Berlin (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Geiger (1856–1943) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Erlangen under Friedrich von Spiegel, later holding professorships at Erlangen (1891) and the University of Munich (1920–1924).

Wilhelm Grube (1855–1908) was a sinologist, linguist, and Tibetologist. He studied under Vasily Vasiliev and Anton Schiefner at St. Petersburg and earned a PhD at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz, later becoming an associate professor of sinology at Berlin in 1892.
Wilhelm Gundert (1880–1971) was a scholar in Japanology and religious studies who succeeded Karl Florenz and held a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1936 to 1945.
